record.paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
record.original_question: In semiclassical black-hole evaporation, a massive star collapses to a black hole with an event horizon; quantum fields near the horizon produce Hawking radiation, and an outside observer can access only the emitted radiation after tracing over interior degrees of freedom. The exterior radiation is described as thermal or mixed, while quantum mechanics requires unitary evolution of pure states. Can the evaporation process be described so that the full quantum state remains unitary and the information about matter that formed or perturbed the black hole is recoverable from the final exterior state, rather than being lost?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a semiclassical model of gravitational collapse and black-hole evaporation in which a massive body collapses to form a black hole bounded by an event horizon, and quantum fields propagating on the resulting curved spacetime produce Hawking radiation at infinity. An asymptotic exterior observer has access only to the radiation degrees of freedom; the interior degrees of freedom (those causally disconnected behind the horizon) are traced out, yielding a reduced density matrix on the exterior that, in the standard Hawking calculation, is thermal (mixed) and depends only on a few macroscopic parameters (mass, charge, angular momentum) of the initial collapsing matter. Quantum mechanics, on the other hand, demands that the global evolution of an initially pure state remain unitary, so that the final state after complete evaporation should also be pure and should encode all information about the initial matter configuration and any subsequent perturbations.

Problem: Provide a mathematically consistent description of the entire formation-and-evaporation process — including a precise specification of the global Hilbert space, the in/out state spaces, and the evolution map between them — such that:
(i) the total evolution from the initial collapsing-matter state to the final post-evaporation state is unitary;
(ii) any pure initial state evolves to a pure final state supported on the exterior radiation Hilbert space after the black hole has fully evaporated; and
(iii) the information characterizing the initial matter (and any infalling perturbations) is recoverable, in principle, from the final exterior quantum state via some explicit decoding map.

Equivalently, determine whether such a unitary, information-preserving description exists, and if so exhibit it; otherwise prove that no such description is compatible with the standard semiclassical assumptions (locality of effective quantum field theory outside the horizon, validity of general relativity in low-curvature regions, and the equivalence principle near a smooth horizon).
artifact.status_search_result: The black hole information problem remains a central open question in theoretical physics. Significant progress since 2019–2020 via the "island formula" and replica wormhole computations has reproduced a unitary Page curve for the radiation entropy in certain semiclassical gravitational path-integral calculations, providing strong evidence consistent with unitarity. However, a complete, mechanism-level resolution—an explicit unitary map and information-recovery protocol within a fully consistent semiclassical (or quantum-gravitational) framework—is not established, and the problem is widely regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Replica wormholes and the entropy of Hawking radiation
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the Page curve via replica wormholes, giving entropy consistent with unitary evaporation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent semiclassical computations recover a unitary Page curve, evidence for unitarity but not a full resolution.

status_evidence.title: The entropy of Hawking radiation (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews island formula and remaining open questions about how information is encoded in Hawking radiation.
status_evidence.claim: Authors describe the mechanism of information recovery as still incompletely understood.

status_evidence.title: Black hole information paradox - overview
status_evidence.snippet: The paradox remains a major unresolved problem in theoretical physics, although recent work supports unitarity.
status_evidence.claim: Widely characterized as an open problem.
